#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cases for the ghostty/powerlevel10k prompt-corruption guard: the line in
# zsh.nix that primes `_ghostty_saved_ps1` so ghostty's zsh integration skips its
# newline-marking pass.
#
# Why this one line gets a test when the rest of the prompt does not: its logic
# is a model of somebody else's code. It works by pre-setting variables private
# to ghostty's `ghostty-integration`, so that script's own `ps1_changed` guard
# fires on the first precmd instead of missing it. A comment asserting that is
# worth nothing -- if upstream renames those variables or changes the `${var+x}`
# gate the guard reads, nix still builds, `hms` still succeeds, and the only
# symptom is a literal `}}` reappearing before the prompt char.
#
# The mechanism being guarded: ghostty marks continuation lines by rewriting PS1
# as text, `PS1=${PS1//$'\n'/$'\n'${mark2}}`. Under PROMPT_SUBST a prompt is
# code, not text -- p10k's PROMPT is one nested parameter expansion holding
# newlines as data inside `${...}` -- so the `}` in the spliced mark closes an
# expansion a level early and the braces after it fall out as literal text.
# Upstream still does this on `main`: PR #11596 renamed the mark from
# `133;A;k=s` to `133;P;k=s` but kept both the substitution and the guard, so the
# bug and this workaround both outlive it.
#
#   ./tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh        # drives the cases against the live config
#   ./tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh <dir>  # against some other ZDOTDIR
#
# It reads a *generated* config (the live `~/.config/zsh` by default), so it
# tests what `hms` actually switched in rather than what zsh.nix says. Before the
# first switch carrying the fix it skips rather than fails, and says why.
#
# Both startup paths are covered, because they are genuinely different and only
# one of them is obvious:
#   - injected: ghostty spawns the shell with ZDOTDIR pointed at its own
#     directory, whose .zshenv sources the user's and then the integration.
#   - plain: no injection, and the integration arrives only via the
#     `source .../ghostty-integration` line home-manager writes into .zshrc.
set -u

ZD="${1:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/zsh}"

# --- preconditions ------------------------------------------------------------
# Every one of these is a skip, not a failure: none of them means the guard is
# broken, and a red suite for "ghostty is not installed here" trains people to
# ignore the suite.
skip() { echo "SKIP: $*"; exit 0; }

GRD="${GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR:-}"
if [ -z "$GRD" ]; then
  # Not running under ghostty; find the resources dir next to the binary.
  gb=$(command -v ghostty) || skip "no ghostty on PATH and GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR unset"
  GRD="$(dirname "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$gb")")")/share/ghostty"
fi
GZ="$GRD/shell-integration/zsh"
[ -r "$GZ/ghostty-integration" ] || skip "no ghostty zsh integration under $GZ"
[ -r "$ZD/.zshrc" ] || skip "no .zshrc in $ZD"
grep -q 'powerlevel10k' "$ZD/.zshrc" || skip "$ZD/.zshrc does not load powerlevel10k"
grep -q '_ghostty_saved_ps1' "$ZD/.zshrc" ||
  skip "$ZD/.zshrc has no _ghostty_saved_ps1 priming -- run hms first (zsh.nix carries it)"
command -v script >/dev/null || skip "util-linux script(1) not available"

D=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
trap 'rm -rf "$D"' EXIT

# --- the two configs ----------------------------------------------------------
# `with` is the live config verbatim; `without` is the same config with the
# priming deleted. Deriving the negative case from the positive one is what keeps
# this honest -- it cannot pass by failing to exercise the bug, because the
# `without` cases assert the corruption IS there once the line is gone.
for v in with without; do
  mkdir -p "$D/$v"
  for f in .zshrc .zshenv .p10k.zsh; do
    if [ -r "$ZD/$f" ]; then cp "$ZD/$f" "$D/$v/$f" && chmod u+w "$D/$v/$f"; fi
  done
  # Repoint ZDOTDIR and the p10k config at the copy, or the copy would load the
  # originals and both variants would end up identical.
  if [ -r "$D/$v/.zshenv" ]; then
    sed -i "s|^export ZDOTDIR=.*|export ZDOTDIR=\"$D/$v\"|" "$D/$v/.zshenv"
  fi
  sed -i "s|~/.config/zsh/.p10k.zsh|$D/$v/.p10k.zsh|g" "$D/$v/.zshrc"
done
sed -i '/typeset -g _ghostty_saved_ps1/d' "$D/without/.zshrc"

# A harness that silently stopped differentiating the two configs would report
# "all passed" forever, so check the setup itself before trusting any case.
grep -q 'typeset -g _ghostty_saved_ps1' "$D/with/.zshrc" ||
  { echo "harness bug: priming missing from the 'with' copy" >&2; exit 1; }
if grep -q 'typeset -g _ghostty_saved_ps1' "$D/without/.zshrc"; then
  echo "harness bug: priming survived in the 'without' copy" >&2; exit 1
fi

# --- runner -------------------------------------------------------------------
# A pty is mandatory: p10k renders nothing recognisable on a pipe, and the
# artifact only exists in a real prompt render. Six commands, so a regression
# that only shows after the first prompt still lands.
render() { # <with|without> <injected|plain>  -> raw pty output, control chars visible
  local v=$1 mode=$2
  # shellcheck disable=SC2054 # the commas are inside one env value, not separators

# dotfiles

Home Manager configuration for `sauyon`.

## New machine setup

For a blank machine (ISO, disk, base Arch install), see
[docs/new-host.md](docs/new-host.md). The steps below assume Arch is already
running.

```bash
# 1. Clone into ~/devel/dotfiles
mkdir -p ~/devel
git clone https://github.com/sauyon/dotfiles ~/devel/dotfiles

# 2. If this is a new host, add a homeConfigurations entry for it in flake.nix
#    (hostname, gui, gpu). Otherwise the matching entry already exists.

# 3. Install Nix
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf -L https://install.determinate.systems/nix \
  | sudo sh -s -- install --no-confirm

# 4. Source Nix and trust mise
. /nix/var/nix/profiles/default/etc/profile.d/nix-daemon.sh
mise trust ~/devel/dotfiles/mise.toml

# 5. Apply (flake attr matches hostname)
nix run github:nix-community/home-manager -- switch --flake ~/devel/dotfiles#$HOST
```

After the first switch, `home-manager switch` is available directly.

## Applying changes: `hms`

`hms` is the normal way to switch. It does **not** build locally by default — it
pushes, waits for the commit's CI run, then switches, which turns the switch into
a download of the closure the runner already built and pushed to attic.

```bash
hms              # push, wait for the run, then switch
hms --local      # skip CI and build here (the old `home-manager switch` alias)
```

Things it deliberately refuses rather than works around:

- **A dirty tree.** CI builds a pushed commit, so an uncommitted switch is one CI
  can never reproduce. Commit, or use `--local`.
- **A stale checkout.** If `origin/master` has commits you do not, it says so and
  stops — rebasing is your call, and waiting on a run for a SHA that is not
  `origin/master` would be waiting on the wrong build.

It falls back to a local build, with a note, when the host has no CI job (mari)
or when the commit touched nothing `nix-home.yml`'s `paths:` filter matches. On a
red run it prints the job's actual `error:` lines, not just a status.

Why this is worth a wait: see `docs/ci-nix-home.md`. The short version is that
the runner has far more of everything than these boxes, and its output is
bit-identical to what a local build would produce.

## Tests

Nothing here has a suite; the exception is anything whose logic is a model of
someone else's, where a comment claiming the model is right proves nothing.

```bash
./tests/hyprlock-faillock.sh     # builds the script, then drives 33 cases
./tests/system-packages.sh       # sources system/pacman.sh, drives 21 cases
./tests/thermald-setup.sh        # drives 8 cases against system/thermald-setup
./tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh   # drives 13 cases against the live generated zsh config
./tests/steam-ui-scaling.sh      # evaluates 3 hosts, drives 4 cases
./tests/hyprland-zen-popup.sh    # drives 7 cases against the live generated hyprland.lua
```

`hyprlock-faillock` (in `home.nix`) reproduces pam_faillock's two tally windows
to tell the lock screen whether the account is locked out. The cases drive the
real built script through its `FAILLOCK_BIN` / `FAILLOCK_CONF` / `FAILLOCK_USER`
seams, so a stub reader supplies synthetic tally records -- no real failed
logins, no waiting out a real ten-minute lockout.

`system/pacman.sh` holds the parts of `system/deploy`'s package convergence that
model someone else's rules: the list format plus the per-host overlay, and the
single `Include` line appended to `/etc/pacman.conf` (whole-line matched, so the
stock config's commented-out examples don't read as "already enabled"). The
cases source it and run against a temp tree through its `SUDO` seam, then hand a
copy of this host's real `pacman.conf` to `pacman-conf` to confirm pacman does
glob an `Include` and does register a `[multilib]` section reached through one --
the assumption the whole drop-in design rests on. Nothing writes to `/etc`, and
no case needs root.

`system/thermald-setup` (run from `system/deploy`) is the *enable* half that a
package list cannot express: `pacman -S` installs a unit, it does not start one.
Which hosts want thermald is decided upstream of it, by `thermald` appearing in
`system/packages.<host>` — so the script's own gate is just "is it installed",
and a host whose list never asked for it is one it never touches. The cases drive
the real script with stub `pacman`/`sudo`/`systemctl` on `PATH`, asserting both
halves: a host without the package does nothing at all, and a converged host
escalates zero times.

The `_ghostty_saved_ps1` priming in `zsh.nix` is a model of ghostty's
`ghostty-integration`: it pre-sets variables private to that script so its own
`ps1_changed` guard fires on the first precmd, which is what stops the PS1
rewrite that corrupts powerlevel10k's `PROMPT` into a literal `}}`. Rename those
variables upstream and nix still builds, `hms` still succeeds, and the only
symptom is the artifact coming back. The cases render the *live generated* config
in a pty -- both the injected and plain startup paths -- and assert the `}}` is
gone with the line and still returns without it, so a workaround that has quietly
stopped working fails out loud, and so does one that has become unnecessary.

`STEAM_FORCE_DESKTOPUI_SCALING` (in `home.nix`) models Steam's side of a bargain
Hyprland can't enforce: `xwayland.force_zero_scaling` hands X11 clients real
pixels and no DPI hint, and Steam's CEF UI reads neither `Xft.dpi` nor
`GDK_DPI_SCALE`, so on a scaled panel it draws tiny until told its own factor.
The cases evaluate three hosts and derive every expectation from the config
itself — the var must equal the scale that host's eDP-1 monitor rule asks for,
and be unset where there is no such rule — so the pair can't drift apart
silently, which is the only way this fails. A fourth case asserts a scaled host
still exists, since otherwise all three would pass vacuously.

## System config

Files under `system/` mirror `/` and require root to deploy:

```bash
system/deploy
```

`system/packages` is the pacman list every Arch host must satisfy;
`system/packages.<hostname>` is layered on it for one box (shiori's `steam` and
its 32-bit drivers). Deploy converges pacman onto both on every run, and enables
multilib via `system/etc/pacman.d/conf.d/multilib.conf` plus one `Include` in
`/etc/pacman.conf`. A newly enabled repo has no sync db, so the first deploy
after this asks for a `sudo pacman -Syu` rather than refreshing behind your back
(`-Sy` without the `-u` is the partial-upgrade footgun).

## Storage tuning

One-shot tuning for the btrfs-on-LUKS-on-loop-on-ext4 home stack: sets LUKS
workqueue-bypass flags, `noatime` on host `/home`, grows btrfs into LUKS
device slack. Idempotent. The LUKS step prompts for the passphrase.

```bash
system/storage-tuning.sh
```

## Secrets (sops-nix)

Secrets are decrypted using `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` as an age identity. On a new machine, either copy your existing key or generate one and add it as a sops recipient:

```bash
# Add new machine key as recipient
cd ~/devel/dotfiles
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
mise run sops -- updatekeys secrets.yaml
```

input.content:
tests: the ghostty mark2 case asserted something that cannot happen

The continuation-line case has been red since it landed: `injected: expected a
continuation-line mark without the priming, got 0`. The guard it belongs to is
fine -- every other case passes, `}}` is still absent with the priming and still
returns without it. What was wrong is the case.

It asserted that dropping the priming lets ghostty's mark2 reach the terminal,
making the priming a real if small trade. That cannot happen on a p10k prompt,
and the reason is the bug this whole file exists to pin. mark2 is
`%{\e]133;A;k=s\a%}`; splicing it after a newline inside p10k's PROMPT puts its
`%}` inside a `${...}`, which is what closes the expansion a level early. The OSC
escape is then sitting inside an expansion that has already been cut short, so it
is consumed along with it rather than printed. The `}}` the two cases above
assert IS that escape's wreckage. The mark cannot both corrupt the prompt and
survive it, so it renders 0 with the priming and 0 without -- which also means
the case above it, "suppressed with the priming (0)", was passing vacuously.

Measured against ghostty 1.3.1, whose integration still uses the A spelling:

                          with   without
  '}}'                       0         1
  133;A;cl=line (mark1)      6         6
  133;A;k=s     (mark2)      0         0
  133;P;k=i     (fallback)   5         5

The marks block only runs on the first prompt -- from the second on, p10k owns
the tail of precmd_functions, ghostty's `precmd_functions[-1] == _ghostty_precmd`
test fails, and it falls back to the zle-line-init path that emits 133;P;k=i when
PS1 carries no mark. So there is exactly one prompt where the splice can happen,
and exactly one `}}` to show for it.

So the two cases become one, and it asserts the thing that is true and worth
knowing: the priming costs no continuation-line mark, because there was never a
mark to lose. Written as an equality rather than as "both are 0" so it stays a
comparison -- if upstream moves the splice somewhere that survives a p10k prompt,
`without` goes positive while `with` stays 0, and this fails instead of quietly
agreeing.

The teeth are unchanged and still elsewhere: the two `}}`-returns-without-the-
priming cases are what fail if the workaround stops being necessary.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

You are a READ-ONLY security reviewer. Write nothing — no files, no git commands that mutate, no edits. Report findings only.

Repo: /home/sauyon/devel/dotfiles/.drovr/wt/ghostty-contline (a git worktree; stay inside it).
Review range: `git diff 4362f0a..HEAD` — commit b007ea8, which touches only `tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh` and `README.md`.

Context: this is a personal dotfiles repo. `tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh` is a bash test harness that copies the user's live generated zsh config into a temp dir, deletes one line from the copy, and renders both variants in a pty via `script -qc 'zsh -i'` to compare terminal escape-sequence output. The change under review replaced two assertions about a ghostty OSC "continuation-line mark" with a single equality assertion, and edited comments plus a README paragraph.

Review as a skeptic, not as the author. Specifically look for:
- Unsafe temp-file/temp-dir handling: predictable paths, missing cleanup, TOCTOU, symlink attack surface in the mktemp/trap/cp/sed flow.
- Command injection or unquoted expansion where a path (e.g. $D, $ZD, $GZ, $HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME) containing spaces, newlines, or shell metacharacters would break out — including inside the `sed -i "s|...|...|"` substitutions and the `env`/`script -qc` invocation.
- Anything that writes outside the temp dir, or that could modify the user's REAL ~/.config/zsh rather than the copy. This matters most: the harness `chmod u+w`s and `sed -i`s files it copied — confirm it can never touch the originals.
- Secrets or identifying data (this repo is public and has a strict no-email-addresses rule) being written into the test, README, or any output the test prints.
- Whether the change weakened a security-relevant assertion.

Note the base commit already contained most of this harness; judge the DIFF, but flag a pre-existing issue if the diff's lines depend on it — say clearly which is which.

Rate every finding Critical, Important, or nit. If you find none, say so explicitly. Report as a list; for each: file, line, severity, one-sentence defect, and a concrete failure scenario (inputs -> bad outcome). Do not propose patches.

  ## Verdict
  
  **No Critical findings. No security vulnerability in the diff.** The specific thing you flagged as mattering most — whether the harness can modify the user's real `~/.config/zsh` — I verified end-to-end and it **cannot**. Details in the "Verified safe" section below.
  
  I found one Important correctness/consistency defect introduced by the diff, one Important pre-existing defect that the diff's own lines depend on, and three nits.
  
  ---
  
  ## Findings
  
  ### 1. `zsh.nix:300` — **Important** (correctness; pre-existing text, but the diff is what makes it wrong)
  
  The diff rewrote the test and README to claim the priming costs *zero* continuation-line marks, but left the authoritative source comment in `zsh.nix` stating the exact opposite — it still reads `one continuation-line mark (`133;A;k=s`, 1 -> 0)`. This is not a pre-existing issue I'm flagging gratuitously: it was *true and consistent* before commit b007ea8 and is *false and contradictory* after it, because the diff changed the claim in two of the three places that carry it.
  
  Failure scenario: a future reader (or agent) opens `zsh.nix` to decide whether the priming line is still worth keeping, reads "this costs you one mark on the first prompt," and weighs a trade-off that the test now asserts does not exist. Conversely, someone reading the new test comment's confident "there was never a mark to lose" and then finding the `1 -> 0` measurement in `zsh.nix` has no way to tell which was measured and which was reasoned. One of the two is an empirical claim someone recorded from a real run; the diff does not say which one it invalidated or why the earlier measurement was wrong.
  
  Note the diff's own commit message ("asserted something that cannot happen") argues from mechanism, not from a new measurement. The old assertion `mark2_without -gt 0` presumably passed at some point, which is where the `1 -> 0` number came from. If it never passed, the README's previous "13 cases" line implies the suite was green with it, which is worth reconciling.
  
  ### 2. `tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh:103-104` (inside `render()`) — **Important** (pre-existing; the diff's new lines 164-165 depend on it)
  
  **This is the one real "writes outside the temp dir" finding, and it is pre-existing.** `render()` runs `zsh -i` with `ZDOTDIR` pointed at the temp copy, but `HOME` is left pointing at the real home, and the copied `.zshrc` hardcodes an absolute history path that the harness's two `sed -i` passes do not rewrite:
  
  - live `.zshrc:59`: `HISTFILE="/home/sauyon/.local/share/zsh/history"`
  - live `.zshrc:60`: `mkdir -p "$(dirname "$HISTFILE")"`
  - live `.zshrc:69`: `SHARE_HISTORY` is set
  
  Failure scenario: running `./tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh` performs 8 `render` calls, each feeding `true / cd /tmp / true / print hi / cd - / exit` into an interactive zsh that appends all of it to the user's **real** shell history — roughly 40 junk entries per test run, plus `SHARE_HISTORY` causing those shells to read and re-import the real history. The same path also reaches `ZSH_CACHE_DIR` writes (`.zshrc:288`, `mise completion zsh >| "$ZSH_CACHE_DIR/completions/_mise"`) and the p10k instant-prompt cache under `~/.cache` (`.zshrc:154-155`). The harness's isolation story is "point ZDOTDIR at a copy," which isolates *config reads* but not *absolute-path writes* the config performs.
  
  This is squarely pre-existing (the `render` function is untouched by b007ea8), but I'm rating it Important rather than nit because the diff's two new lines 164-165 are `render` calls and you asked specifically about writes outside the temp dir.
  
  ### 3. `tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh:166` — **nit** (weakened assertion; *not* security-relevant)
  
  You asked whether the change weakened a security-relevant assertion. It did not — this assertion is about terminal escape-sequence parity, not a security control. But it did weaken a *liveness canary*, which is worth naming since the diff's own comment claims the opposite.
  
  The replaced pair contained an implicit self-check: `[ "$mark2_without" -gt 0 ]` could only pass if the pty actually rendered a prompt. The new `[ "$mark2_with" = "$mark2_without" ]` passes vacuously when the harness measures nothing at all, because `count()` returns `0` for empty input (`grep -o` matches nothing, exits 1, `wc -l` prints 0).
  
  Failure scenario: a zsh/ghostty/`script(1)` change makes `render` produce no usable output (integration silently not sourced, `zsh -i` dying early, `script -qc` behavior change). Both counts are `"0"`, `"0" = "0"` is true, and the case reports `ok injected: priming costs no continuation-line mark (with=0 without=0)` — green on a dead measurement. The comment at lines 155-159 asserts this design "fails rather than quietly agreeing," which is true only for the one scenario it names (upstream moving the splice so `without` goes positive) and false for the dead-harness scenario.
  
  Mitigating: cases at lines 140-141 (`braces ... gt0`) are separate renders that *would* fail if nothing rendered, so the suite as a whole retains a canary. That's why this is a nit and not Important.
  
  ### 4. `tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh:76,78` — **nit** (pre-existing; sed metacharacter injection via `TMPDIR`)
  
  `$D` is interpolated into the *replacement* half of two `sed -i "s|...|...|"` expressions unescaped. `mktemp -d` honors `TMPDIR`, so `$D` is not fully under the script's control.
  
  Failure scenario: `TMPDIR='/tmp/a|b' ./tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh` → `$D` contains the `|` delimiter → `sed: -e expression #1, char N: unknown option to 's'`, and (with no `set -e`) the script continues with an unrewritten `.zshrc`. A `&` in `TMPDIR` would instead expand to the matched text inside the replacement, silently producing a wrong path. Not exploitable — anyone who controls your `TMPDIR` already controls your environment — and the diff does not touch these lines. Flagging only because you asked about the `sed -i "s|...|...|"` flow specifically.
  
  ### 5. `tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh:61` — **nit** (pre-existing; trap coverage)
  
  `trap 'rm -rf "$D"' EXIT` covers normal exit but not `INT`/`TERM`/`HUP`. Bash usually runs the EXIT trap on an untrapped SIGINT, but it will not on SIGKILL or when the terminal goes away mid-`script(1)`. Failure scenario: killing a hung pty render leaves a `0700` temp dir with copies of your zsh config in `/tmp` until reboot. Low impact precisely because the dir is `0700` and contains only a copy of already-world-readable nix-store config.
  
  ---
  
  ## Verified safe (things you asked about that check out)
  
  **The harness cannot touch the real config.** I traced this concretely rather than taking the comments' word for it:
  
  - The live files are symlinks into the nix store (`/home/sauyon/.config/zsh/.zshrc -> /nix/store/6946i6d...-home-manager-files/.config/zsh/.zshrc`, mode `r--r--r--`). This is the dangerous shape — if the copy stayed a symlink, `chmod u+w` (which follows symlinks) would target the store file.
  - Line 71 uses plain `cp` with no `-a`/`-d`/`-P`, so it **dereferences**: `$D/$v/.zshrc` is a fresh regular file with a new inode. `chmod u+w` and `sed -i` therefore act on the copy only. The store originals are unreachable from every write in the script.

content.content:
## NO EMAILS

**Never write an email address into anything.** Not into files, commit messages,
docs, notes, handoffs or scratch files — mine, colleagues', or service accounts.
This repo is public, and an address is a durable identifier that spreads: it
leaks the work/personal boundary, it enumerates people, and once written it gets
copied onward.

Refer to an account by its **role** — "the personal Google account", "the work
account", "the project's GCS service agent" — or record the command that
recovers the identity at read time (`gcloud config get-value account`) rather
than pasting its output. Role-based wording is better documentation anyway: "must
be the personal account, not the work one" survives an address change; a pasted
address does not.

If an address seems genuinely load-bearing, ask first.

The exception is the git identity already configured in `home.nix`, which git
requires and which is on every commit regardless.

## Commit and Push Policy

This is a personal dotfiles repo on `master`. When asked to commit and push, do both without asking for confirmation. The global "ask before public communications" rule does not apply here.

## Applying config: use `hms`, not `home-manager switch`

`hms` (defined in `home.nix`, documented in `README.md`) pushes, waits for the
commit's CI run on `forge.ko.ag`, then switches — so the switch is a download of
the closure the in-cluster runner built, not a local compile. Expect it to block
for ten-odd minutes. `hms --local` builds here instead.

It refuses on a dirty tree and on a checkout behind `origin/master`. **Both
refusals are the feature.** CI can only build a pushed commit, so do not route
around them with a bare `home-manager switch` — commit and push, or pass
`--local` deliberately and say that you did.

If a run goes red, `hms` prints the job's `error:` lines; read those rather than
re-running blind. Background on why CI is worth waiting for — and the 600s attic
transfer ceiling that made it unreliable for its first 61 runs — is in
`docs/ci-nix-home.md`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cases for the ghostty/powerlevel10k prompt-corruption guard: the line in
# zsh.nix that primes `_ghostty_saved_ps1` so ghostty's zsh integration skips its
# newline-marking pass.
#
# Why this one line gets a test when the rest of the prompt does not: its logic
# is a model of somebody else's code. It works by pre-setting variables private
# to ghostty's `ghostty-integration`, so that script's own `ps1_changed` guard
# fires on the first precmd instead of missing it. A comment asserting that is
# worth nothing -- if upstream renames those variables or changes the `${var+x}`
# gate the guard reads, nix still builds, `hms` still succeeds, and the only
# symptom is a literal `}}` reappearing before the prompt char.
#
# The mechanism being guarded: ghostty marks continuation lines by rewriting PS1
# as text, `PS1=${PS1//$'\n'/$'\n'${mark2}}`. Under PROMPT_SUBST a prompt is
# code, not text -- p10k's PROMPT is one nested parameter expansion holding
# newlines as data inside `${...}` -- so the `}` in the spliced mark closes an
# expansion a level early and the braces after it fall out as literal text.
# Upstream still does this on `main`: PR #11596 renamed the mark from
# `133;A;k=s` to `133;P;k=s` but kept both the substitution and the guard, so the
# bug and this workaround both outlive it.
#
#   ./tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh        # drives the cases against the live config
#   ./tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh <dir>  # against some other ZDOTDIR
#
# It reads a *generated* config (the live `~/.config/zsh` by default), so it
# tests what `hms` actually switched in rather than what zsh.nix says. Before the
# first switch carrying the fix it skips rather than fails, and says why.
#
# Both startup paths are covered, because they are genuinely different and only
# one of them is obvious:
#   - injected: ghostty spawns the shell with ZDOTDIR pointed at its own
#     directory, whose .zshenv sources the user's and then the integration.
#   - plain: no injection, and the integration arrives only via the
#     `source .../ghostty-integration` line home-manager writes into .zshrc.
set -u

ZD="${1:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/zsh}"

# --- preconditions ------------------------------------------------------------
# Every one of these is a skip, not a failure: none of them means the guard is
# broken, and a red suite for "ghostty is not installed here" trains people to
# ignore the suite.
skip() { echo "SKIP: $*"; exit 0; }

GRD="${GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR:-}"
if [ -z "$GRD" ]; then
  # Not running under ghostty; find the resources dir next to the binary.
  gb=$(command -v ghostty) || skip "no ghostty on PATH and GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR unset"
  GRD="$(dirname "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$gb")")")/share/ghostty"
fi
GZ="$GRD/shell-integration/zsh"
[ -r "$GZ/ghostty-integration" ] || skip "no ghostty zsh integration under $GZ"
[ -r "$ZD/.zshrc" ] || skip "no .zshrc in $ZD"
grep -q 'powerlevel10k' "$ZD/.zshrc" || skip "$ZD/.zshrc does not load powerlevel10k"
grep -q '_ghostty_saved_ps1' "$ZD/.zshrc" ||
  skip "$ZD/.zshrc has no _ghostty_saved_ps1 priming -- run hms first (zsh.nix carries it)"
command -v script >/dev/null || skip "util-linux script(1) not available"

D=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
trap 'rm -rf "$D"' EXIT

# --- the two configs ----------------------------------------------------------
# `with` is the live config verbatim; `without` is the same config with the
# priming deleted. Deriving the negative case from the positive one is what keeps
# this honest -- it cannot pass by failing to exercise the bug, because the
# `without` cases assert the corruption IS there once the line is gone.
for v in with without; do
  mkdir -p "$D/$v"
  for f in .zshrc .zshenv .p10k.zsh; do
    if [ -r "$ZD/$f" ]; then cp "$ZD/$f" "$D/$v/$f" && chmod u+w "$D/$v/$f"; fi
  done
  # Repoint ZDOTDIR and the p10k config at the copy, or the copy would load the
  # originals and both variants would end up identical.
  if [ -r "$D/$v/.zshenv" ]; then
    sed -i "s|^export ZDOTDIR=.*|export ZDOTDIR=\"$D/$v\"|" "$D/$v/.zshenv"
  fi
  sed -i "s|~/.config/zsh/.p10k.zsh|$D/$v/.p10k.zsh|g" "$D/$v/.zshrc"
done
sed -i '/typeset -g _ghostty_saved_ps1/d' "$D/without/.zshrc"

# A harness that silently stopped differentiating the two configs would report
# "all passed" forever, so check the setup itself before trusting any case.
grep -q 'typeset -g _ghostty_saved_ps1' "$D/with/.zshrc" ||
  { echo "harness bug: priming missing from the 'with' copy" >&2; exit 1; }
if grep -q 'typeset -g _ghostty_saved_ps1' "$D/without/.zshrc"; then
  echo "harness bug: priming survived in the 'without' copy" >&2; exit 1
fi

# --- runner -------------------------------------------------------------------
# A pty is mandatory: p10k renders nothing recognisable on a pipe, and the
# artifact only exists in a real prompt render. Six commands, so a regression
# that only shows after the first prompt still lands.
render() { # <with|without> <injected|plain>  -> raw pty output, control chars visible
  local v=$1 mode=$2
  # shellcheck disable=SC2054 # the commas are inside one env value, not separators
  local -a e=(GHOSTTY_SHELL_FEATURES=cursor:blink,path,title)
  if [ "$mode" = injected ]; then
    e+=(ZDOTDIR="$GZ" GHOSTTY_ZSH_ZDOTDIR="$D/$v")
  else
    e+=(ZDOTDIR="$D/$v")
  fi
  printf 'true\ncd /tmp\ntrue\nprint hi\ncd -\nexit\n' |
    env "${e[@]}" script -qc 'zsh -i' /dev/null 2>&1 | cat -v
}

count() { grep -o "$1" | wc -l | tr -d ' '; } # <grep -o pattern>, text on stdin

n=0
fails=0
ok() {
  n=$((n + 1))
  echo "  ok    $*"
}
bad() {
  n=$((n + 1))
  fails=$((fails + 1))
  echo "  FAIL  $*"
}

braces() { # <desc> <variant> <mode> <eq0|gt0>
  local out b
  out=$(render "$2" "$3")
  b=$(printf '%s' "$out" | count '}}')
  case "$4" in
  eq0) if [ "$b" -eq 0 ]; then ok "$1"; else bad "$1 (expected no '}}', got $b)"; fi ;;
  gt0) if [ "$b" -gt 0 ]; then ok "$1"; else
    bad "$1 (expected '}}' to appear, got $b -- these cases no longer exercise the bug)"
  fi ;;
  esac
}

# --- the guard holds ----------------------------------------------------------
braces "injected: no '}}' with the priming" with injected eq0
braces "plain:    no '}}' with the priming" with plain eq0

# --- the cases above still mean something -------------------------------------
# If either of these goes quiet, upstream changed something and the two cases
# above have stopped testing anything. That is a failure, not a pass.
braces "injected: '}}' returns without the priming" without injected gt0
braces "plain:    '}}' returns without the priming" without plain gt0

# --- what the priming actually costs: nothing the terminal ever sees ----------
# Skipping the newline pass means the continuation-line mark it splices is never
# spliced. The obvious next thought -- that the mark therefore reaches the
# terminal without the priming, and so the priming trades a real feature away --
# is wrong here, and wrong for the reason the whole workaround exists.
#
# On a p10k PROMPT the splice is what breaks the expansion. mark2 is
# `%{\e]133;A;k=s\a%}`, and its `%}` closes a `${...}` a level early; the OSC
# escape sits inside the expansion that just got cut short, so it is consumed as
# part of the wreckage rather than printed. The `}}` the two cases above assert
# IS that wreckage. The mark cannot both corrupt the prompt and survive it.
#
# So the count is 0 in both variants, and that is the assertion: the priming
# costs no mark, because there was never a mark to lose. Measured as equality
# rather than as "both are 0" so it stays a comparison -- if upstream ever moves
# the splice somewhere that survives a p10k prompt, `without` goes positive,
# `with` stays 0, and this fails rather than quietly agreeing.
#
# `[AP]` because upstream renamed this mark from `133;A;k=s` to `133;P;k=s` in
# PR #11596: on a ghostty that predates the rename it is the A spelling, after it
# the P one, and this case should hold across the bump either way.
mark2_with=$(render with injected | count '133;[AP];k=s')
mark2_without=$(render without injected | count '133;[AP];k=s')
if [ "$mark2_with" = "$mark2_without" ]; then
  ok "injected: priming costs no continuation-line mark (with=$mark2_with without=$mark2_without)"
else
  bad "injected: priming changed the continuation-line mark count (with=$mark2_with without=$mark2_without)"
fi

# --- nothing else is lost -----------------------------------------------------
# The point of priming the guard rather than dropping ghostty's integration
# (which also silences the `}}`, at the cost of the cursor sequences and half the
# title writes) is that everything else still works. Compare the variants mark
# for mark. `133;A;cl=line` rather than a bare `133;A`: the latter also matches
# the continuation-line mark above on a pre-#11596 ghostty, which made this probe
# read as a regression when it was measuring the intended difference.
inj_with=$(render with injected)
inj_without=$(render without injected)
for probe in '133;A;cl=line' '133;B' '133;C' '133;D' '\^\[\[[0-9] q' '\^\[\]2;' 'file://'; do
  a=$(printf '%s' "$inj_with" | count "$probe")
  b=$(printf '%s' "$inj_without" | count "$probe")
  if [ "$a" = "$b" ]; then
    ok "injected: '$probe' count unchanged by the priming ($a)"
  else
    bad "injected: '$probe' count changed by the priming (with=$a without=$b)"
  fi
done

echo
if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "all $n cases passed"
else
  echo "$fails of $n cases FAILED"
fi
exit $((fails > 0))

# Repointing ZDOTDIR isolates config *reads*, not the writes the config then
  # performs to absolute paths baked in as literals. HISTFILE is the one that
  # bites: with SHARE_HISTORY every probe shell appends its six commands to the
  # real shell history and reads the real history back in, so a plain run of this

  # the harness measures nothing. Isolating the writes that persist is the whole

  sed -i "s|^HISTFILE=.*|HISTFILE=\"$D/$v/history\"|" "$D/$v/.zshrc"
done

# That rewrite is what keeps the suite off the real history, so prove it landed
# rather than trusting it -- a silent miss here is invisible until the history is
# already dirty.
for v in with without; do
  grep -q "^HISTFILE=\"$D/$v/history\"" "$D/$v/.zshrc" ||
    { echo "harness bug: '$v' copy still writes the real shell history" >&2; exit 1; }
done

input.command:
git add -A && git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
tests: stop the ghostty harness writing the real shell history

Review of the previous commit turned up two things, one of which it caused.

zsh.nix recorded the priming's cost as "one continuation-line mark
(`133;A;k=s`, 1 -> 0)". The previous commit changed that claim in the test and
the README and left the authoritative copy saying the opposite, which is worse
than either version alone: a reader deciding whether the priming still earns its
keep had no way to tell which number was measured. Reconciled, and the fact that
the number moved is recorded rather than quietly corrected -- every other count
in that comment (mark1 6, B/C/D 6/6/5, cursor 18, title 24, cwd 6) still
reproduces exactly, so it was measured, and the conditions that produced the 1
have not been recovered.

The other is older and worse. Repointing ZDOTDIR isolates where the config is
read from, not where the config then writes. `HISTFILE` is a literal absolute
path in the generated .zshrc, and SHARE_HISTORY is set, so every probe shell
appended its six commands to the real shell history and read the real history
back in -- 48 junk entries per run of this file, and the six at the tail of the
history right now are from running it. Repointed at the temp tree, with the
rewrite asserted rather than assumed, since a silent miss is invisible until the
history is already dirty.

Only HISTFILE, deliberately. Giving the probe shells a fresh HOME and XDG dirs
also works and is tidier, and it breaks the suite: with no p10k instant-prompt
cache the shell renders a different PROMPT, the `}}` stops reproducing, and both
teeth cases go quiet. Isolating the writes that persist is the fix; isolating the
reads changes the thing under test. The failing run is in the commit history of
this branch if it needs re-deriving.

Also: the new mark2 case compared two counts that are both 0, which is also what
an empty render produces, so it would have gone green on a dead harness. It now
requires each render to have drawn a prompt before the equality counts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git log --oneline -2 && git show --stat --format="" HEAD

1	# dotfiles
2	
3	Home Manager configuration for `sauyon`.
4	
5	## New machine setup
6	
7	For a blank machine (ISO, disk, base Arch install), see
8	[docs/new-host.md](docs/new-host.md). The steps below assume Arch is already
9	running.
10	
11	```bash
12	# 1. Clone into ~/devel/dotfiles
13	mkdir -p ~/devel
14	git clone https://github.com/sauyon/dotfiles ~/devel/dotfiles
15	
16	# 2. If this is a new host, add a homeConfigurations entry for it in flake.nix
17	#    (hostname, gui, gpu). Otherwise the matching entry already exists.
18	
19	# 3. Install Nix
20	curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf -L https://install.determinate.systems/nix \
21	  | sudo sh -s -- install --no-confirm
22	
23	# 4. Source Nix and trust mise
24	. /nix/var/nix/profiles/default/etc/profile.d/nix-daemon.sh
25	mise trust ~/devel/dotfiles/mise.toml
26	
27	# 5. Apply (flake attr matches hostname)
28	nix run github:nix-community/home-manager -- switch --flake ~/devel/dotfiles#$HOST
29	```
30	
31	After the first switch, `home-manager switch` is available directly.
32	
33	## Applying changes: `hms`
34	
35	`hms` is the normal way to switch. It does **not** build locally by default — it
36	pushes, waits for the commit's CI run, then switches, which turns the switch into
37	a download of the closure the runner already built and pushed to attic.
38	
39	```bash
40	hms              # push, wait for the run, then switch
41	hms --local      # skip CI and build here (the old `home-manager switch` alias)
42	```
43

content.content:
6c24bd2309748a5f91b67124d79d5545b64d3c9d
zsh: fix the ghostty prompt test, which was testing one path twice

d451aaf shipped this test red and its comment wrong. Both came from the same
mistake, so they are fixed together.

script(1) runs its `-c` command through $SHELL. Mine is zsh, so the outer
non-interactive zsh read ghostty's .zshenv first -- which rewrites ZDOTDIR and
unsets GHOSTTY_ZSH_ZDOTDIR while skipping the integration, its `always` block
gating on `interactive` -- and the inner `zsh -i` never got the handoff. Every
case labelled `injected` was silently running the plain path. Proof, with the
.zshrc source line neutralised so only injection can load the integration:

  SHELL=/bin/zsh -> _ghostty_state unset, no precmd
  SHELL=/bin/sh  -> _ghostty_state set, precmd installed

With the paths actually separated, the picture is different from what d451aaf
recorded. The artifact is plain-path only: the integration is sourced from
.zshrc after p10k, so its precmd is last and it takes the PS1-rewriting branch.
Under real ZDOTDIR injection it loads at .zshenv time, before p10k, its precmd
is not last, it prints marks directly and never rewrites PS1 -- no artifact
there, and the priming is inert. Measured, 6-command session:

  path      priming  braces  mark1  B  C  D  cursor  osc2  osc7
  injected  with        0      5    6  6  5    18     24     9
  injected  without     0      5    6  6  5    18     24     9
  plain     with        0      6    6  6  5    18     24     9
  plain     without     1      6    6  6  5    18     24     9

So f26bbf5's "counts identical with and without" was right and d451aaf's
"correction" to it was wrong: there is no suppressed continuation-line mark,
`133;[AP];k=s` is 0 in every cell. That claim came from a coarse `133;A` probe
read against a home-manager generation other than the one being reasoned about.
The comment is corrected and the false case is gone.

What the test does now:
- Drives the two paths distinctly, SHELL=/bin/sh for the injected one.
- Checks that they ARE distinct before trusting anything else, via a third
  config copy whose source line is neutralised: injected must load the
  integration, plain must not. Conflating them is the bug being fixed here, so

# three from the live config is what keeps this honest -- it cannot pass by
# failing to exercise the bug, because a case below asserts the corruption IS
# there once the priming is gone.
for v in with without nosrc; do
  mkdir -p "$D/$v"
  for f in .zshrc .zshenv .p10k.zsh; do
    if [ -r "$ZD/$f" ]; then
      cp "$ZD/$f" "$D/$v/$f"
      chmod u+w "$D/$v/$f"
    fi
  done
  # Repoint ZDOTDIR and the p10k config at the copy, or it would load the
  # originals and the variants would collapse into one.
  if [ -r "$D/$v/.zshenv" ]; then
    sed -i -e "s|^export ZDOTDIR=.*|export ZDOTDIR=\"$D/$v\"|" "$D/$v/.zshenv"
  fi
  sed -i -e "s|~/.config/zsh/.p10k.zsh|$D/$v/.p10k.zsh|g" "$D/$v/.zshrc"
done
sed -i -e '/typeset -g _ghostty_saved_ps1/d' "$D/without/.zshrc"
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # the $ is literal: it is in the .zshrc being matched
sed -i -e 's|^  source "\$GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR"/shell-integration/zsh/ghostty-integration$|  :|' \
  "$D/nosrc/.zshrc"

# A harness that stopped differentiating the variants would report "all passed"
# forever, so check the setup itself before trusting a single case.
setup_bug() {
  echo "harness bug: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}
grep -q 'typeset -g _ghostty_saved_ps1' "$D/with/.zshrc" ||
  setup_bug "priming missing from the 'with' copy"
! grep -q 'typeset -g _ghostty_saved_ps1' "$D/without/.zshrc" ||

input.new_string:
sed -i -e "s|~/.config/zsh/.p10k.zsh|$D/$v/.p10k.zsh|g" "$D/$v/.zshrc"
  # Repointing ZDOTDIR isolates where the config is read from, not where the
  # config then writes. HISTFILE is a literal absolute path in the generated
  # .zshrc and SHARE_HISTORY is set, so without this every probe shell appended
  # its six commands to the real shell history and read the real history back in
  # -- a plain run of this file left dozens of junk entries behind.
  #
  # Only HISTFILE, deliberately. Giving the probe shells a fresh HOME and XDG
  # dirs is tidier and breaks the suite: with no p10k instant-prompt cache they
  # render a different PROMPT, the artifact stops reproducing, and the cases that
  # assert it go quiet. Isolating the writes that persist is the fix; isolating
  # the reads changes the thing under test.
  sed -i -e "s|^HISTFILE=.*|HISTFILE=\"$D/$v/history\"|" "$D/$v/.zshrc"
done

tests: keep the ghostty prompt harness out of the real shell history

Repointing ZDOTDIR isolates where the config is read from, not where the config
then writes. HISTFILE is a literal absolute path in the generated .zshrc and
SHARE_HISTORY is set, so every probe shell this file starts appended its six
commands to the real shell history and read the real history back in on the way.
A plain run left dozens of junk entries behind; the tail of the history on this
box is still `true / cd /tmp / true / print hi / cd - / exit` from running it.

Repointed at the temp tree, with the rewrite asserted for all three copies rather
than assumed -- a silent miss here is invisible until the history is already
dirty, which is the failure mode that let this run unnoticed since d451aaf.

Only HISTFILE, deliberately. Giving the probe shells a fresh HOME and XDG dirs
also works, is tidier, and breaks the suite: with no p10k instant-prompt cache
they render a different PROMPT, the `}}` stops reproducing, and the cases that
assert it go quiet. Isolating the writes that persist is the fix; isolating the
reads changes the thing under test.

Verified by running the suite with the probe command carrying a unique token: 13
cases pass and the token appears zero times in the real history.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git log --oneline -2

Done, and one thing I stopped on.

**Blocked — I did not run `hms`.** Local `master` has 12 unpushed commits from another session: WIF/TPM device keys, revocation tooling, `secrets.yaml`, `.sops.yaml`. `hms` pushes before it switches, so applying my one-line test fix would publish all of that. Not mine to publish.

**Shipped to the branch `ghostty-histfile` (commit `d5ca97f`):** the harness no longer writes your real shell history. `HISTFILE` is a literal absolute path in the generated `.zshrc` and `SHARE_HISTORY` is on, so every probe shell was appending to the real history and reading it back. Their 13 cases pass; a run with a unique token in the probe command puts zero entries in the real history. Two clean review rounds, all four angles each.

**History stripped:** 244 harness blocks, 1464 of 2199 lines — two-thirds of the file. 734 real entries remain. Backup at `~/.local/share/zsh/history.bak-20260928-142639`.

**Your other session won the race on the original bug, and was more right than me.** They found that `script -qc` runs through `$SHELL`, so every case labelled `injected` was silently running the plain path — the real root cause. I'd only established that the mark2 assertion was unsatisfiable. I dropped my commit for theirs and kept only the part they didn't cover.

Two caveats:

1. Any zsh still running from before the strip will rewrite the file from its in-memory copy on exit and restore those entries. Close old shells, or re-run the strip afterwards.
2. `master` moved five times during this task and another session is actively editing this exact test file, so `d5ca97f` may need a rebase before it lands.

**Next:** run `git log --oneline origin/master..master` — when that comes back empty, their work is pushed and I can merge `ghostty-histfile` and run `hms` cleanly.
